QF.id: SEBI Guidelines for AML Standards, CFT and PF with KYC Norms_8

question.text: What should a registered intermediary do when it suspects that performing the CDD process will "tip off" the client?

answer.text: Not pursue the CDD process and instead file a Suspicious Transaction Report (STR) with FIU-IND
Continue the CDD process and inform the client about the suspicion
Close the client's account immediately without any reporting
Wait for SEBI to give specific instructions before taking any action

explanation.text: The Logic: When the intermediary suspects that performing CDD will tip off the client, it should NOT pursue the CDD process. Instead, it must file a Suspicious Transaction Report (STR) with FIU-IND within 7 days of arriving at the conclusion that the transaction is suspicious, while maintaining strict confidentiality. The Trap: Never inform the client about the suspicion — tipping off is prohibited before, during, and after STR submission. Do not close the account unilaterally and do not wait for SEBI instructions; the source-prescribed action is to file the STR with FIU-IND within the 7-day timeline. Note: If, during re-KYC, further questioning would alert the client, stop questioning and quietly escalate to the Principal Officer so the STR can be filed within 7 days of forming the suspicion. Continue normal dealing with the client to avoid tipping off.
